title: stackward transaction state v1
description: The state of the current access-critical transaction, at /var/lib/stackward/transaction.json (mode 0600), written atomically and only under the run lock. stackward apply writes it before it arms the rollback timer; the timer's rollback, stackward undo --transaction and stackward confirm change it. One transaction at a time: a new one replaces the file once the old one is confirmed, aborted or its rollback acknowledged. Adding an optional field is not a breaking change; removing or renaming a field, or changing a meaning, needs transaction.v2.

id.description: The run id of the apply run; its journal is /var/backups/stackward/<id>/journal.json.

status.description: open: applied and validated, waiting for stackward confirm until the deadline. confirmed: the change stays. rolled-back: undone. rollback-failed: the undo failed part way. aborted: the timer could not be armed and nothing changed. Access-critical steps are refused while the status is open, and while it is rolled-back or rollback-failed without acked_at.

steps.description: The step ids of the transaction.

deadline.description: When the rollback timer fires, RFC 3339 UTC.

confirm_within.description: The --confirm-within duration, as Go prints it (5m0s).

timer_unit.description: The transient systemd units, NAME.timer and NAME.service.

rollback.description: The command the timer runs: the root only copy of stackward under /var/lib/stackward/transactions/<id>/ with undo --transaction <id> --yes --by-timer.

confirmed_via.description: new-ssh-session: confirmed from a session that differs from the one that applied. console: confirmed with --console, the provider console path.

cause.description: Why it rolled back: timer, validation, apply-failed or manual.

error.description: Why the rollback or the arming failed.

acked_at.description: When the rollback was acknowledged (stackward confirm --ack-rollback). A rollback the person watched (validation, apply-failed, manual) is acknowledged when it happens.

session.description: The facts that tell one login session from another. Every field is absent when it could not be read.

ssh_connection.description: SSH_CONNECTION: client address, client port, server address, server port. From the environment, or from the login shell when sudo dropped it.

audit_session.description: /proc/self/sessionid, the kernel audit session opened at login (kept across sudo and su).

login_uid.description: /proc/self/loginuid, the user who logged in. Recorded, not compared.

sshd.description: The per session sshd process this command descends from, as PID:START (start time in clock ticks after boot).
